name: YTDL-Material Capture
description: Captures media URLs and the request headers that made them work, then sends them to a YoutubeDL-Material instance.

content_security_policy.//: The Manifest V3 default is "script-src 'self'; upgrade-insecure-requests;" - that last directive rewrites every http:// request from an extension page to https://, at the CSP layer, before the network stack is involved. Material is typically a self-hosted service on a LAN address with no certificate, so the upgrade meets a plain-HTTP port, the TLS handshake fails with SSL_ERROR_RX_RECORD_TOO_LONG, and fetch reports a bare NetworkError with nothing reaching the server and no webRequest error event to inspect. It is invisible on localhost, which upgrade-insecure-requests skips as potentially trustworthy - so it only appears once Material is somewhere other than the same machine. This policy is the default minus that directive; nothing here is relaxed beyond it.
